steps.name: Lively Staffer
steps.text: Hey! Been to the printing house now they've refurbished it?

steps.name: Curious Staffer
steps.text: No, I haven't. What about it?

steps.name: Lively Staffer
steps.text: I went with someone to see yesterday, and it blew my mind.

steps.name: Lively Staffer
steps.text: Everything in there's brand-new, and the sheer amount of space! Nothing like the crappy little place it used to be.

steps.name: Lively Staffer
steps.text: Look, their manager gave me a sample. Look at their print quality now.

steps.name: Curious Staffer
steps.text: Oh, wow, this paper... and the type is so detailed... How did they get this good?!

steps.name: Lively Staffer
steps.text: Right? It pumps me up just knowing whatever we write, they're turning into books!

steps.name: Curious Staffer
steps.text: Really? What a blessing—think how out of date their place used to be. Almost unusable.

steps.name: Lively Staffer
steps.text: You're telling me! And the manager's thrilled too. Says they'll chew right through it no matter how much we ask to print.

steps.name: Curious Staffer
steps.text: Hahaha, we'd better not fall behind then! We don't want to waste printing this good with bad writing.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I'm here! Sorry, the kitchen was a little short-handed this morning.

steps.name: Lively Staffer
steps.text: Gosh, hi there, Kjarr.

steps.name: Lively Staffer
steps.text: You should hear yourself, though. Aren't head maids busy enough? You shouldn't have to go to all this trouble for us, we'll be fine.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Oh, but I should. I went and asked the Saintess for this job—I'd be furious at myself if I was sloppy.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Plus, she has a lot of interest in the Kjerag Guidebook. It's part of how the outside sees our lovely place, you know.

steps.name: Lively Staffer
steps.text: We were saying! Ooh, doesn't it just feel like Kjerag gets a little better every day these days? Our crew can't be falling behind now.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Is there another Tri-Clan Council meeting today?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: They can't help it. Victoria's position is a major hassle.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: My. So we're finally reaping what Enciodes sowed over there.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: At this point, it's all we can do to think on our feet.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Oh, Kjarr.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: There's something I want us to discuss.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I'd like to make an appointment with Her—

steps.name: Lively Staffer
steps.text: Kjarr? Kjarr? Hello, are you in there?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Hm? Oh, I'm fine. Come to mention, where's our dear old Chief of Tourism? He hates even the mention of falling behind.

steps.name: Lively Staffer
steps.text: Huh, true. Kaj's barely ever late.

steps.name: Fretful Wife
steps.text: Is this the Department for Tourism?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Who might you be?

steps.name: Lively Staffer
steps.text: Oh, aren't you Kaj's wife?

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Yes, yes! Oh, wonderful, I found the right place.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: What's the matter? You look pale.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Could you let me meet the Saintess? It's urgent business.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: What happened?

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: You're Head Maid Kjarr, aren't you, the one always by her side?

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Oh, thank Kjeragandr! It's about my spouse, you see.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: He's always hated the idea of my son studying abroad, but my son doesn't like to back down either. He's been pulling the tuition fee together all on his own, without my spouse knowing, so he can go still.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: I... *sigh* I'm soft at heart. He asked me to hide it from Kaj, and so I did.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Kjeragandr knows how, but Kaj found out anyway. He's off to the station now to catch the boy.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: He's a temperamental one, he is, but my boy's no less. If they let this become a full-on fight, I—honestly, I don't know what I'll even do with myself.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Kjarr, could you please ask the Saintess to help us?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: She isn't staying atop Mount Karlan today. I'm afraid it'd be too late to find her there, even if I do go.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Wh—Well, now what?!

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Oh, it's all my fault! If I could've just stopped Kaj for a second...

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Here. I'll go with you.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: One of my duties is standing in to split the Saintess's load, you know.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: In cases like this, I can deliver some words in the Saintess's name.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Right, right, right, of course. All us townsfolk know how close you and her are, Madam Head Maid. I'm sure whatever you say would reach them.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: We'll want to hurry, then. I'd have to guess Kaj's already at the station by now.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Mm. Let's go.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Oh, by Kjeragandr, how do we find Kaj in a station this busy—

steps.name: Chief Kaj
steps.text: I'VE TOLD YOU AND I'VE TOLD YOU AGAIN! You'll have NO thoughts of foreign schooling as long as I live and breathe!

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I think he's saved us the search.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Heavens, there's a crowd already! He'll be the laughing stock of the neighbors.

steps.name: Youth
steps.text: And I'll keep saying it back, I'm going to this school, and that's final.

steps.name: Chief Kaj
steps.text: Genuinely, it's beyond me where you got this malarkey about being 'advanced' into your head.

steps.name: Youth
steps.text: It would be beyond you. All you care about is your faith—oops, no, I mean, how to work your so-called 'faith' to your own benefit.

spans.text: be beyond you. All you care about is your faith—oops, no, I mean, how to work your so-called 'faith' to your own benefit.

steps.name: Chief Kaj
steps.text: YOU SHUT YOUR MOUTH!

steps.name: Chief Kaj
steps.text: You sneak off to the station without telling your own father, and now the nerve to talk to me like this! Aren't you embarrassed enough?!

steps.name: Youth
steps.text: What, me? You're the embarrassing one here, Chief Kaj of Tourism!

steps.name: Chief Kaj
steps.text: You horrid little—!

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Please, Kjarr! Anything, quick!

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: (*sigh* The mettle in Enya to handle these issues every single day. Let me leave... Let me go back to she who swore to split the Saintess's load, because I have a nice round slap to give her.)

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: (I may as well say something or other. Enya can take the rest after that.)

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Kjarr?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: *sigh* Very well—

steps.name: Youth
steps.text: So what? If you can't get what you want from Grandpa, you'll settle for making me in your image instead?

steps.name: Chief Kaj
steps.text: YOU SAY THAT ONE MORE TIME!

steps.name: Youth
steps.text: Do you know where Grandpa is right now?

steps.name: Chief Kaj
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Youth
steps.text: No, no you don't.

steps.name: Youth
steps.text: You've never understood him.

steps.name: Chief Kaj
steps.text: I don't understand him? HE doesn't understand ME!

steps.name: Youth
steps.text: Hmph, keep telling yourself that. I'm not giving my whole life to the mountain weeds and rubble he way he did, but I actually LIKE Grandpa.

steps.name: Youth
steps.text: I'll go and I'll learn all that advanced stuff, then I'll come back and help him, and once I do, he can polish Kjeragandr's claws that much faster and easier.

steps.name: Youth
steps.text: I'm not like you, stepping on everything he's left behind, everything everyone before him left behind, just so you can climb on up!

steps.name: Chief Kaj
steps.text: YOU—

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Sorry, can I just check who Kaj's father—

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: His pappsen? Odd man, spends all year up in the mountains hammering away, rarely even comes home.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: They were already on awful terms when I married Kaj. I'd like to get along with him, but I've never found the chance.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: One time while drunk, Kaj said that apparently, my in-law's under the impression he's doing Kjeragandr's fingernails, and that's why he stays up in the mountains all the time.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: ...So what does Kaj think?

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: He... He says he'll never follow his pappsen's example as long as he lives.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Calls him a moron, says he hasn't the first about faith.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Well, then.

steps.name: Chief's Wife
steps.text: Kjarr, where are you going? Didn't you say you'd step in and help?!

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I have someone better for the job.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: (Mutter) ...At least, maybe.
By one means or another, as they grow, most people of Kjerag come to know the names of the mountains that surround this place we call Kjerag.
For one reason or another, they'll set foot into those mountains for themselves, but always the more well-known ones.
The ones no one talks of... those are seldom intruded, even by locals of the land.
Yet the mountain Kjarr scales now is one of the unnoted—a peak so obscure it was never even named, a height you wouldn't assume anyone dwelt on.
And if anyone else is on this mountain path at this moment, she might frankly be a little surprised.
For a very simple reason. Aside from the peaks Karlan Trade promotes for sightseeing, no mountain's paths could claim to be as smooth as this one's.
—No, even the most tourist-magnet peaks struggle to have paths this pristine.
Yes. Pristine.
The trees are trimmed, the grass seems to grow in its designated place, and there are no loose rocks to be found.
It's practically a garden.
Halfway up, a crisp clanking drifts down from on high. It's fast one moment, slow the next, reverberating through the valley, as if a giant sits in the pass hammering his weapon out.
Kjarr remembers this sound.
When she reaches the summit, so too is the sound's source revealed.
He is no giant, and what he beats is no weapon at all.
He's but a lone, wizened hunchback, chipping a hammer and chisel away at a prominent jut of stone.
The old man, his hammer and chisel, everything comes off dwarfed compared to that stone. Not that he seems to mind. He simply carries on hammering, chiseling.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Phew...
For some reason, Kjarr lets out what feels like a sigh of relief.
And thereafter, she takes a set of spare tools from the side, draws next to the old man, and together with him, begins to chip away at the looming stone.
He asks nothing, and Kjarr says nothing.
The silence is no awkward one, but instead brings on a kind of mutual understanding, one that defies words.
Chisel, then hammer. Chisel, then hammer.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: *huff*—
He remains silent, and simply shuffles to the side, where from his rucksack he pulls a swig of water.
After that, he takes out two lovingly parchment-wrapped grain cakes, and hands one of them over to Kjarr.
Kjarr hardly refuses. Taking it, she sits down beside him and digs in.
The old man unwraps the other cake, meanwhile, and begins to devour it in great bites.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: What is it you're doing here?

steps.name: Old Man
steps.text: What are you here for, if you don't know?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: It looked like fun.

steps.name: Old Man
steps.text: For generations, our family has done but one thing, and that is trim Kjeragandr's Claws for Her.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Claws...? You mean, the fingernails?
He lifts his head, and jabs a finger at those faraway peaks, the loftiest and most endless of them all. Then he points to their neighbors, a run of peaks that seem quite modest in comparison.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: Those ranging mountains are Her Back. All those little peaks that bulge up alongside them, those are Her 'Claws'.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Well, isn't Kjeragandr a woman? They're erecting a statue of her on the lake island right now.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: That is the human form She takes to reach out to Her people. That, yes, is Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: But these mountains, too, these are Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: My ancestor witnessed it. The scene. There in the black rains was She, and cast forth divine might, and rose a shield to protect the people of Kjerag.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: And in the end, She was victorious, but paid a hefty price.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: Grateful for Her protection, my ancestor sought to tend to Her Claws.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: And so, that became your family tradition.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: If word of any of this got out, I worry the entire Vine-Bead Court would trip head over heels to meet you.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: I assume you came in my son's place, girl.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: Go and tell him. I will not give him what my forebears left behind.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I'm not your son's messenger.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I just feel it's a shame. It seems like neither your son nor your grandson plan to take up your mantle.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: ...Hammering away in the mountains is all I've known, all my life.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: I did assume Kaj would follow after me, just as I did after my pappa, but—before I even realized it, he became this way.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: I'm bad at words, and I had no idea what to do, so into the mountains I went to hide.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: *sigh*.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: If I remember correctly, Kaj turns forty this year.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: His childhood was right when the last Silverash head, Olafur, came back from study abroad...

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Mmm. You probably remember. That's when they started building these railroad whatever-you-call-its.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: But you probably didn't know that Olafur brought back more than technologies. He brought ideologies.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: His free-thinking brought Kjerag into total dispute around then. And I've no doubts that out of them all, it was the young who were most easily impacted.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I think... it must have struck Kaj deeply.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: But his family was generationally bound to tend to Kjeragandr's nails.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I can only imagine he found himself quite trapped.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I can't know what thoughts he had after that, or what actions he took—

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: But perhaps, by thinking along those lines, you can figure out what made him the way he is now.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: Damn me.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: No. It's not your fault.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: You took on your hammer and chisel from your father, and your father took them on from his father, all the way back to your ancestor—

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: You've all been devoutly, wholeheartedly doing what you had to do. What mistake was it that you ever made?

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: You see—

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Your grandson says he plans to go and learn a few new things, all so you can better polish Kjeragandr's claws.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: ...Noah, the boy, always visits me.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: But the things, that he gets for me, those communicating terminal sorts of machines, I don't understand them one bit.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Do you truly hate these new things?

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: I watch as they lay the railroad bit by bit from east to west, and I watch as they build their tall buildings bit by bit ever taller.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: If it was true that Kjeragandr didn't like it, She would have but to roll over to shake it all off.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: I... trust Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Well, keep trusting in her, then.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: There's one thing I can promise you.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: If Kjeragandr does roll over and get up from the mountains one day, then those fingernails you've tended to will be the part of Her that glitters most.
Watching Kjarr depart, her back turned, the old man is hit with a sudden sense of familiarity.
For an age, he sifts through his mind. And finally, he realizes. Her appearance is akin, in ways, to that of the figure passed down by his ancestor in tradition.

The one who walked and saw a land of deep disaster, who walked and saw despair twined with grief, who walked and saw branches bud in the thawing frost, who walked and saw the warming sun. The one who brought hope to Kjerag.
A streak of bewilderment flashes through the old man's clouded eyes.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: By Kjeragandr, by Kjeragandr.
He pulls the comms terminal from his grandson out of his pocket.
Though he can't get used to it, he's made an effort to learn, in order to make his grandson happy.
In the terminal are saved two numbers. One is home. One is his grandson's. He calls the latter.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: Noah. Yes, it's me.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: Kaj is there, isn't he?

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: Tell him for me, I'll give him what he wants.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: But, he must let you go.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: Yes, that's alright.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: Good. Now, give the terminal to him.

steps.name: Nail-Tender
steps.text: I have to talk to him—
After just a few steps, without knowing why, Kjarr comes to a standstill.
She lifts her head and looks to the mountain range afar. At some point, a strange stone has floated to her side.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: My, my, silly you.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Could you imagine saying any of that back in those times?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Kaj's faith, devout yet blind. Noah's drive, zestful yet reckless.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: And Dag, that type of human you once appreciated—

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: How many nights you laid in the mountains' cradle, lulled to sleep by the sound of clinks and clanks.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Silly you. You forgot how to be grateful, and talked Dag's ear off to boot. Now you've done it. Who could like you after this?
Kjarr cups the stone in her hands, her tone as if resentful at the person behind it, yet in some way as if looking in a mirror.
The stone subtly trembles, then begins to sound.
It is her voice.

steps.name: Hovering Stone
steps.text: My, my, silly you.

steps.name: Hovering Stone
steps.text: You still won't admit just how much you've changed, ever since getting to know the girl?

steps.name: Hovering Stone
steps.text: You have friends, now. A berth, now. Wants, now. As naturally as natural comes, you have a standpoint now.

steps.name: Hovering Stone
steps.text: Isn't that the one thing you used to hate most?

steps.name: Hovering Stone
steps.text: Didn't you always hope the Kjerags would go on to live with minds of their own?

steps.name: Hovering Stone
steps.text: Wasn't keeping watch over them all you wanted to do?

steps.name: Hovering Stone
steps.text: Silly you, and this family of Silverashes too, for tormenting you so!

steps.name: Hovering Stone
steps.text: Babbling about hope, blathering about future, making a sorry fool out of you!
The plateau's hoary winds sweep through the ranges, and on with a brush past her lobes. To her ears, it is the sound of Her laughing.
A touch teasing, a touch mocking, a touch self-defeated, a touch helpless.
Who is She laughing at? None but Herself, of course.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: If you want to bring up friends, you're guilty of making some yourself back then.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: If you want to bring up relationships, you've never once been able to stop yourself getting involved.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: You want to help, yet you tell me I shouldn't lay a finger.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: You feel they're wrong, yet you think they should arrive at their own judgments.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Silly you. Can you honestly not tell why she was the one?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Is she so special she'd stand alone for an eon before and after?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Or just, plain and simple, she's done for you what you always wanted?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjarr, where are you?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I'm... You'd have no idea even if I told you.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I'll take that. I hear you showed yourself and solved a little issue for me?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Oh, my. Word does get around to you fast, Saintess.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I don't care to hear, but they keep insisting I do anyway.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Tell me what's on your mind, Saintess.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: How are you feeling about my question from before?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: What question? Your dinner tonight?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjarr, I'm not asking as a joke!

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: The appointment?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Victoria's about to send their people here.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Once they arrive, I want Her not to get involved, no matter what happens.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: It's not the time for Her to act yet, is it?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: If we can't even make it through this little crisis ourselves, well, I'll just go and dive into Lake Silberneherze.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Good grief. You really put your brother's stubbornness to shame at times, you know.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: And thank you very much for saying that.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Will you be back at the Vine-Bead Court tonight?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: I'm on my way back now. I have your dinner to make, Saintess—I can't be dilly-dallying.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Just a hunch, but are you in a good mood?

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Is it that obvious to you?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: After how long we've known each other? Of course.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: It's nothing much, just saw nice weather today and went for a little walk.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Good evening.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Mm-hm. Good evening.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Pfft. My, my, silly me.
A laugh like bells takes to the wind, and on with brush after brush past the mountaintops. This time, it's her laughing.
She lingers no longer, and sets off for Mount Karlan.
It's time she got home—there's work waiting for her.
